title: Early Zapotec glyphic inscriptions at San José Mogote and Monte Albán
summary: Monument 3 at San José Mogote, Oaxaca, shows a nude captive with two glyphs read as a day name in the Zapotec 260-day calendar, among the earliest signs of Mesoamerican writing. Later captive carvings, the Danzantes at Monte Albán, carry true linear texts. Dating Monument 3 is disputed, from about 600 BCE to as late as 200 BCE.

uncertainty.note: Marcus (1992) dates Monument 3 to c. 600 BC; Cahn and Winter (1993) argue for as late as 200 BC or later. Writing that probably encodes Zapotec is dated as early as 500 BC at Monte Albán.
